The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 4.5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn on this record's stable key from the stocks its household class may hang (4.5 in or 5 in; T-1839, docs/LIBERTIES.md L352), then advanced within them so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

land_owner.value: The ground was entered by Robert A Kenzie, 7 May 1831
land_owner.note: KINZIE'S ADDITION. The north fraction of section 10 is the section north of the river, which is why the register prints 102.29 acres and not a quarter's 160. It is resolved as the section's own grid box clipped to the committed north bank of the main stem (`e1834_harbor_cut/shoreline.geojson`), so no boundary here is authored. The two rows the register carries for it — one plain, one with the school-section marker — are the same entry printed twice. THE REGISTER SPELLS THE PURCHASER MORE THAN ONE WAY for this same tract — Robert A Kenzie; Robert A Kinzie — and the spellings are carried rather than merged, which is the land_sales crosswalk's standing rule: tract agreement is where two spellings MIGHT be one man and is never proof that they are. THE ROOF IS AN INVENTION AND THIS CANNOT OUTRANK IT. The footprint stands 35 m inside the tract's nearest boundary, which on a documented building would carry the middle tier, but this building was dealt to its lot by a recipe and is not there. The tract is real and the register's words about it are read; what is graded here is the claim that THIS roof stands on it, and that claim is the recipe's. WHAT THIS ROW CLAIMS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It claims that the tract the Illinois State Archives' land-sale register describes contains this structure's committed position — the patent for this ground was ENTERED by this man on this date. It does not claim he still held the ground on 1 July 1835, that he lived here, or that he ever stood on it: a sale is a transaction, and the register's only column about residence names a county. THE SECTION LINES ARE CONSTRUCTED, NOT TRACED (L219): the grid is carried from the single PLSS corner at State & Madison, on the plat's own east-west bearing, in nominal one-mile squares.

persons.name: Daniel Baxter
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Baxter, Daniel' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 4 — dated 1835-07-01. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

residents.research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). residents.name: The lodgers of Reconstructed H2 medium boarding house #022
residents.why: THE BED IS THE CLAIM. The lodging model puts 8 people in this house on an ordinary night and 18 when it was full, apportioned from the town model's own bracket. These people are here because the beds are, and for no other reason.
residents.basis: BEDS, AND ONE FAMILY. 7 of the people here took a bed and are not kin to each other or to anybody else under this roof — `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one record holds them all. The exception is the keeper and the 3 child(ren) on their card, who are a family and say so: every one of them carries `kin_of` naming the keeper.

persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'South, Orange' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 20 May 1835, column 13 — dated 1835-05-20. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. persons.name: B F Washburn
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented once and corroborated by nothing else, so the weakest rung of `inferred` the owner's ladder defines. A SINGLE APPEARANCE AND NOTHING ELSE. Read from poll_1834. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G3), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. poll_1834 names this person at Chicago by 31 December 1834 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1). THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Washburn, B. F.” (poll_1834_111, line 280). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Washburn' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED / GENERATED, NOT AN ATTESTED NAMED BUILDING. Aggregate mix follows the supplied specification; exact presence, position, footprint, finish and instance-level form are interpretive. H-family boarding-house massing currently uses a generic frame dwelling/block archetype.

fabric_basis.words: ochre-washed clapboard on a balloon frame under a new roof — a merchant's or professional house, new-built (rule F-M: a merchant's or professional man's by its type)

sizes.upper_windows: ceil(18 crowded beds / 3 to a chamber) = 6, held to 5-10 (the house's own five bays to the H3 crosswalk's top) = 6: 6 across the upper storey of the front and of the rear
sizes.stovepipes: ceil(8 ordinary beds / 3 to a stove) = 3, held to 2-6: 3
sizes.chimneys: not sized by the beds: the two brick stacks are the household's kitchen and common-room hearths, and the stoves the beds add go out through the roof as stovepipes

lodging.note: The town model puts a boarding house at 9 people on an ordinary night and 21 when full, from the 1840 household tail (p90 and p99 of 964 Chicago households). This building takes the share of its class's total that its 165 m² of enclosed floor (83 m² × 2 storeys) is of the class's floor area.
lodging.replaceable_by: Any source that states this house's rooms, beds or lodgers on a dated day: an advertisement counting its rooms, a traveller's account of how many it slept, a licence return. A stated capacity retires the apportioned one outright.

occupancy.statement: 8 on this card against an ordinary night's 8 beds: 1 seated here from elsewhere in the layer, where no source gives them a roof, 6 drawn against the order book's lodging buckets for beds that were standing empty, a keeper drawn for a roof this programme raised.
occupancy.keeper_owed: Minted by this stage as the keeper. T-1533 drew this keeper's own children here — 3 of them — out of the book's `under_10` lodging cells, at the size the 1840 histogram gives the household. What is still owed is a SPOUSE, which no rule this project has made can draw for a keeper who is a woman; the ledger's `keeper_families` row states it, and the staffing under a keeper is T-1183's.
